title: How do we build a rectangle with diagonal angles fifty and forty?
description: The same order of drawing is used again, this time for a rectangle whose diagonal divides the opposite angles into fifty degrees and forty degrees. The other part of the corner comes from ninety take away fifty.
teaching_notes: One idea: draw the side, then the given angle at the end where the diagonal starts, and let the perpendiculars finish the rectangle. The second part of the corner is ninety take away the first.

video_script.why: A learner repeats the order of the construction for new angles, using ninety take away the first angle to get the second angle at the corner.
video_script.substitution: the rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC making fifty degrees with the side AB
video_script.anchor: a rough rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC, the angles at A marked 50 degrees and 40 degrees
video_script.payoff_line: The rectangle is ready. The diagonal eigh cee makes fifty degrees with eigh bee and forty degrees with eigh dee.

final_answer.value: rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC making 50 degrees with AB and 40 degrees with AD
final_answer.spoken: the diagonal makes fifty degrees with the first side and forty degrees with the other side

maths_rules: each corner of a rectangle is 90 degrees
the second angle at A is 90 - 50 = 40 degrees
the side lengths are free, since only the angles are given
opposite sides are equal, AB = CD and AD = BC, and all angles are 90 degrees
video_script.design: A rough rectangle ABCD stays at the side. Each step of the construction is drawn in a new colour, and the last step checks the sides and angles.
